posts.style: Design & Aspiration · Coastal · The Sunken Fire Lounge
posts.alt: A Del Mar, San Diego hillside terrace at golden hour behind a coastal-contemporary home with weathered cedar siding and a standing-seam metal roof: a raised stainless-steel spa set in an ivory porcelain terrace, a sunken board-formed concrete lounge with a linear gas fire trough and teak sofas with linen cushions, agave, coastal grasses and Torrey pines, a sliver of ocean on the horizon, and neighboring homes close by stepping down the hillside
posts.hook: The quietest seat on a coastal lot is usually the one you step down into.
posts.caption:
Del Mar gives you the view for free and charges you for it in wind. So the lounge here sits two steps below the terrace, inside its own board-formed concrete walls, where the breeze passes overhead and the fire stays steady.

Above it, the spa is raised rather than buried, a clean stainless vessel that reads like a piece of furniture on the terrace. Everything else stays out of the way: ivory paving that carries the interior floor straight outside, agave and coastal grasses, and Torrey pines doing what they have always done on this hillside.

The selections:
• Diamond Spas stainless-steel spa
• Warming Trends CrossFire linear fire trough in board-formed concrete
• Florim porcelain terrace in ivory
• teak lounge seating with linen cushions
• agave, coastal grasses & Torrey pine

posts.style: Neighborhood · Driveway & Curb Appeal · The Banded Drive
posts.alt: The front of a single-story ranch home in Rancho Bernardo, San Diego, at golden hour, with sand-colored stucco, a clay tile roof and a dark bronze garage door: a wide driveway of warm exposed-aggregate concrete divided into large panels by charcoal paver bands, a mature olive tree casting long shadows, blue agave, kangaroo paw and ornamental grasses in decomposed granite, bronze path lights, neighboring ranch homes close by and inland hills beyond
posts.hook: The lines in a driveway decide whether it reads as a slab or as a design.
posts.caption:
Rancho Bernardo's ranch homes sit low and wide, and the driveway is most of what the street sees. This one keeps the honest material, exposed-aggregate concrete in a warm pebble finish, and gives it structure: charcoal paver bands that break the pour into large panels and line up with the garage and the walk.

The bands do real work too. They give the concrete planned places to move, so the surface ages along the lines we drew instead of ones it picks for itself. The olive tree takes care of the rest every afternoon.

The selections:
• exposed-aggregate concrete drive in a warm tan pebble finish
• Belgard paver bands in charcoal
• mature olive, blue agave, kangaroo paw & ornamental grasses in decomposed granite
• Kichler bronze path lights

Want the front of the house to hold its own? DM “DESIGN”.

posts.style: Seasonal · Craft & Process · After the Rain
posts.alt: A San Marcos, San Diego County backyard just after a winter rain, behind a two-story grey-green board-and-batten home with a stone base: a wet grey paver patio reflecting the clearing sky, a slim linear channel drain along its edge, a dry creek bed of river cobble and boulders planted with blue fescue, agave and dwarf olive, a curved stone seat wall, a wood dining table and a cedar pergola, with neighboring two-story homes close by and chaparral hills beyond
posts.hook: January is when a backyard tells you whether it was graded or just paved.
posts.caption:
San Diego gets most of its rain in a handful of winter days, and those days are the real inspection. Water has to go somewhere. In a yard that was planned, you already know where.

Here the patio falls a quiet few degrees toward a slim channel drain, and the drain hands the water to a dry creek bed that looks like a garden feature eleven months of the year. Cobble and boulders slow it down, the planting takes what it wants, and nothing sits against the house or the neighbor's fence.

This is the part of the work nobody photographs. We draw it first, before a single paver is chosen.

The selections:
• Techo-Bloc Blu 60 paver patio
• linear stainless channel drain
• dry creek bed in river cobble and boulders
• Eldorado Stone seat wall · cedar pergola
• blue fescue, agave & dwarf olive

Got a puddle that shows up every winter? DM “DESIGN”.

posts.alt: A compact North Park, San Diego backyard at golden hour behind a 1920s Craftsman bungalow with dark green shingle siding and tapered porch columns: large-format porcelain pavers with gravel joints, a built-in cedar corner bench with linen cushions against a horizontal cedar fence, a round concrete gas fire bowl, a lemon tree and a tangerine tree in terracotta pots heavy with fruit, a bowl of picked citrus on a teak table, cafe lights overhead, and neighboring bungalows, a palm and power lines close by
posts.hook: January in San Diego: the fire is on and the lemons are ready.
posts.caption:
A North Park lot doesn't give you much, and it doesn't need to. One bench built into the corner, one fire bowl, paving laid large so the space reads bigger than it measures, and two trees in pots that happen to be at their best right now.

Winter is citrus season here, which means the best thing in the yard this month is something you can pick on the way back inside. Small yards reward that kind of thinking: fewer pieces, each one chosen, nothing there to fill space.

The selections:
• Belgard porcelain pavers with pea gravel joints
• built-in cedar bench and horizontal cedar fence
• HPC Fire concrete gas fire bowl
• Meyer lemon & tangerine in terracotta
• cafe lights overhead

posts.style: Trust & Difference · Sport Court · One License, Every Trade
posts.alt: An elevated view at golden hour of a Rancho San Diego family backyard behind a two-story Tuscan-style home with ochre stucco, a stone-clad wing and a clay tile roof: a pickleball court in slate blue and sage green bordered by pavers, a long stone seat wall, a pergola over an outdoor kitchen island with a built-in grill and bar seating, a strip of turf, olive trees and agave on a planted slope, with neighboring tile-roof homes close by on both sides and east county hills beyond
posts.hook: A yard like this is five trades. It should still be one phone call.
posts.caption:
A court, a kitchen, a pergola, a wall, a lawn. Each one is a different trade with its own schedule, and the places where they meet are where most backyards go wrong: the court edge against the pavers, the gas line under the patio, the wall footing beside the turf.

We build as a licensed general contractor (CSLB #1139785), which means our crew and every specialty trade work under one license, on one plan and one schedule. Your project manager is your one point of contact, and ten months after it's finished we come back and walk it again.

By design, not by dispatch. References available on request.

The selections:
• VersaCourt pickleball court
• Belgard paver border and patio
• Eldorado Stone seat wall
• StruXure pergola over a DCS grill island
• SYNLawn turf · olive & agave
